references.text: The same request to travel three days into the wilderness to sacrifice to the Lord, given as an instruction from God to Moses
The beginning of the conversation with Pharaoh where Moses and Aaron ask for permission to hold a feast for the Lord in the wilderness
Moses repeats the request for a three-day journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the Lord
Pestilence (דֶּבֶר) is mentioned as a plague striking Egypt, using the same word found in the threat in 5:3
God identifies Himself as the God of the Hebrews; the same expression 'אֱלֹהֵי הָעִבְרִים' is used
The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, commands again that the people be allowed to go and serve Him in the wilderness
The phrase 'the Lord, the God of the Hebrews' is repeated in the message to Pharaoh
Moses and Aaron confront Pharaoh once more with a message from the Lord, the God of the Hebrews
Sword and pestilence are mentioned together as punishment for disobedience to the covenant, similar to the threat in 5:3
A three-day journey from the mountain of the Lord, parallel to the three-day journey into the wilderness
Repetition of the same divine demand in a later confrontation, emphasizing its unaltered nature.
Pharaoh's compromise attempt (limiting the journey) as a direct response to the request for a three-day trip.
Thematic contrast: the wilderness as the destination for sacrifice (source verse) versus the wilderness as a death trap (here).
